Background | Information

Context Import | How | do | people | communicate | when | it | is | not | convenient | to | speak? | We | communicate | vaguely | and | ambiguously | with | each | other | through | gestures | or | eye | contact | . | Although | the | efficiency | is | low | and | the | error | rate | is | high, | there | is | no | better | way | in | special | occasions | .

Context Import | In | the | same | way, | in | the | field | of | human | - | computer | interaction, | gesture | operations | also | exist | . | We | can | let | the | machine | recognize | different | gestures | , | and | then | execute | the | corresponding | instructions | to | meet | our | needs | . | Of | course, | under | normal | circumstances, | it | is | more | appropriate | to | input | commands | through | the | screen | or | keyboard | and | mouse | .

Context Import | At | present, | the | most | widely | used | gesture | control | is | mobile | devices | such | as | mobile | phones | and | tablets | . | When | you | need | to | light | up | the | screen | or | reject | an | incoming | call, | you | can | use | the | motion | of | waving | your | hand | to | complete | it | . | The | gestures | of | different | devices | will | be | different | .
Knowledge | Introduction

New Knowledge | Unimpeded | roads | are | a | major | prerequisite | for | vehicles | to | run | normally | . | However, | in | the | case | of | power | outages | or | severe | congestion, | road | traffic | lights | cannot | work | normally | . | At | this | time, | traffic | police | need | to | be | on | - | site | to | command | . | Gestures | are | often | used | to | command, | or | traffic | is | conducted | on | the | spot | with | the | sound | of | a | whistle | .

New Knowledge | Traffic | gestures | refer | to | the | gestures | used | by | traffic | police | to | ensure | safe | and | smooth | road | traffic | and | direct | vehicles | in | real | time | . | There | are | altogether | 8 | kinds | of | signals | : | stop, | go | straight, | turn | left, | turn | left | and | wait | to | turn, | turn | right, | change | lanes | slowly, | slow | down, | signal | vehicles | to | pull | over | and | stop | .

New Knowledge | In | addition | to | gestures | outside | the | car, | gesture | - | controlled | cars | have | long | been | born | . | It | is | a | car | that | can | recognize | the | driver's | gestures | . | The | driver | can | issue | instructions | to | the | car | by | making | corresponding | gestures | in | the | car | . | Today | we're | going | to | try | to | make | a | robot | that | recognizes | gestures | .

Practice | | | Programming | logo | 03 | The | Judgment | of | Gesture | When | there | is | no | gesture, | the | robot | moves | forward | slowly | . | Here, | in | order | to | better | receive | gesture | information, | no | waiting | time | is | required | .

Further Reading | In | addition | to | gesture | control | cars, | eye | tracking | technology | has | also | been | applied | to | cars | . | In | order | to | ensure | the | core | solution | of | vehicle | driving | safety, | this | technology | judges | the | driver's | attention | by | monitoring | the | relative | movement | of | the | driver's | eyeballs | . | With | the | continuous | development | of | artificial | intelligence | technology, | the | driving | control | and | driving | safety | of | automobiles | have | been | improved | unprecedentedly | .
